```{r poster-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
if (!requireNamespace("here", quietly=TRUE)) stop("Run source('install_packages.R') first. Missing: here")
here::i_am("Poster_Group36.Rmd")
source(here::here("run_analysis.R"), encoding="UTF-8")
source(here::here("R", "06_metadata.R"), encoding="UTF-8")
group_members <- read_group_metadata(here::here("docs", "group_contributions.csv"))
net_value <- function(name) network$summary$value[match(name, network$summary$metric)]
tex_escape <- function(x) {
  replacements <- c("\\"="\\textbackslash{}", "&"="\\&", "%"="\\%",
    "$"="\\$", "#"="\\#", "_"="\\_", "{"="\\{", "}"="\\}",
    "~"="\\textasciitilde{}", "^"="\\textasciicircum{}")
  vapply(strsplit(as.character(x), "", fixed=TRUE), function(chars) {
    m <- match(chars, names(replacements))
    chars[!is.na(m)] <- replacements[m[!is.na(m)]]
    paste(chars, collapse="")
  }, character(1))
}
manifest <- read.csv(here::here("data", "collection_manifest.csv"),
  colClasses="character", na.strings=c("", "NA"))
complete_manifest <- collection_manifest_complete(manifest, comments)
if (isTRUE(params$final_mode) && (!rq2$row_labels_available || !complete_manifest ||
    !isTRUE(params$group_review_confirmed) || !nzchar(trimws(params$repository_url)) ||
    !group_metadata_complete(group_members))) {
  stop("Complete labels, original provenance, member/repo fields and group review before final poster mode.")
}
no_practice <- rq2$rates[rq2$rates$verification_specific == "FALSE", ]
specific <- rq2$rates[rq2$rates$verification_specific == "TRUE", ]
top_authors <- head(network$node_metrics, 2L)
cluster_sizes <- table(clusters$assignments$cluster)
bridge_rows <- bridge$receiver_rates
bridge_text <- paste(sprintf("C%s: %s/%s (%s\\%%)", bridge_rows$cluster,
  bridge_rows$comments_receiving_reply, bridge_rows$comments,
  formatC(100 * bridge_rows$reply_rate, digits=1, format="f")), collapse="; ")
frequent <- head(text_result$frequencies, 3L)
frequent_text <- paste(sprintf("%s (%s)", frequent$term, frequent$frequency), collapse=", ")

# Native vector figures sized for this poster. All values come from the same
# live result objects as the report; no copied screenshot or hard-coded chart.
poster_dir <- here::here("outputs", "figures", "poster")
dir.create(poster_dir, recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)
poster_plot <- function(filename, draw, width=5.25, height=3.25, pointsize=13) {
  destination <- file.path(poster_dir, filename)
  if (capabilities("cairo")) {
    grDevices::cairo_pdf(destination, width=width, height=height,
      pointsize=pointsize, family="sans")
  } else {
    grDevices::pdf(destination, width=width, height=height,
      pointsize=pointsize, useDingbats=FALSE)
  }
  on.exit(grDevices::dev.off())
  draw()
}
poster_plot("rq1_indicators.pdf", function() {
  d <- text_result$candidate_summary
  d <- d[order(d$n_comments), ]
  labels <- c(reading_inspection="Reading / inspection", execution_testing="Execution / testing",
    static_type="Static / type checks", formal_verification="Formal verification",
    responsibility_ownership="Responsibility /\nownership", understanding_trust="Understanding / trust")
  par(mar=c(3.8, 9.4, 0.5, 0.7), mgp=c(2.1, 0.6, 0), las=1)
  b <- barplot(d$n_comments, horiz=TRUE, names.arg=labels[d$category],
    col="#177B87", border=NA, cex.names=0.9,
    xlim=c(0, max(d$n_comments)*1.40), xlab="Retained comments (non-exclusive)")
  text(d$n_comments+1.2, b,
    sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", d$n_comments, d$percentage), adj=0, cex=0.85)
}, height=3.45, pointsize=12)
poster_plot("rq2_reply_rates.pdf", function() {
  par(mar=c(3.4, 4.7, 0.7, 0.8), mgp=c(2.9, 0.7, 0), las=1)
  d <- rq2$rates
  b <- barplot(100*d$reply_rate, names.arg=c("No specific\npractice", "Specific\npractice"),
    col=c("#9BB7CB", "#177B87"), border=NA, ylim=c(0, 100),
    ylab="Reply rate (%)", cex.names=1.05)
  text(b, 100*d$reply_rate+12,
    sprintf("%.1f%%\n%s/%s", 100*d$reply_rate, d$reply, d$n), cex=1.05)
}, height=2.95)
poster_plot("rq3_diagnostics.pdf", function() {
  d <- clusters$diagnostics
  par(mfrow=c(1,2), mar=c(3.8, 4.2, 2.2, 0.6), mgp=c(2.5, 0.7, 0), cex=0.95)
  plot(d$k, d$mean_silhouette, type="b", pch=16, col="#177B87",
    xlab="Number of clusters (k)", ylab="Mean silhouette", main="Separation", cex.main=1)
  points(d$k[d$selected], d$mean_silhouette[d$selected], pch=15, col="#981C3C", cex=1.5)
  plot(d$k, d$minimum_size, type="b", pch=16, col="#177B87",
    xlab="Number of clusters (k)", ylab="Smallest cluster (n)", main="Balance", cex.main=1,
    ylim=range(c(0, d$minimum_size, 5)))
  abline(h=5, col="#981C3C", lty=2)
}, height=2.55, pointsize=11)
poster_plot("rq4_full_network.pdf", function() {
  par(mar=c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(network$graph, layout=network$layout_full,
    vertex.size=4.2, vertex.color="#177B87", vertex.frame.color="white",
    vertex.label=NA, edge.color="#73838E99", edge.width=0.75,
    edge.arrow.size=0.27, edge.arrow.width=0.65, edge.curved=0.08, margin=0.07)
}, height=4.6)
```

```{=latex}
\posterheader{Responsibility and verification of AI-generated code in online discussions}{Group 36 \quad COMP3020 Social Web Analytics \quad Hacker News discussion corpus}
{\fontsize{13}{16}\selectfont `r tex_escape(paste(group_member_lines(group_members), collapse=" | "))`\par}
\vspace{3mm}
\noindent\colorbox{posterPaleTeal}{\parbox{\dimexpr\textwidth-2\fboxsep\relax}{\fontsize{17}{21}\selectfont
\textbf{Overall question.} How are responsibility and verification of AI-generated code discussed online, and how are these discussions structured through reply interactions?\par\smallskip
\textbf{`r nrow(audit$threads)` selected threads \quad `r nrow(raw)` raw comments \quad `r nrow(comments)` retained comments \quad `r length(unique(comments$author))` authors}
}}
\vspace{5mm}

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{0.239\textwidth}
\postersection{posterGreen}{Data and methods}
The group reports collection with R on `r tex_escape(paste(format(as.Date(unique(manifest$original_collection_date)), '%d %B %Y'), collapse=', '))`. Public Hacker News comments: `r sum(audit$removed$dead)` dead and `r sum(audit$removed$deleted)` deleted records removed. IDs and parent links retained; three threads contribute `r round(100*sum(sort(table(comments$thread_id),decreasing=TRUE)[1:3])/nrow(comments),1)`\% of comments.\par
\textbf{Reply outcome:} at least one direct child comment also retained in the clean corpus.\par
\vspace{3mm}
\postersection{posterBurgundy}{RQ1 \quad What is discussed?}
\textbf{What responsibilities and verification practices are discussed in relation to AI-generated code?}\par
Word counts, six non-exclusive lexical indicators and contextual reading describe the discussion.\par
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{outputs/figures/poster/rq1_indicators.pdf}\par
\postercaption{Figure 1. Candidate mentions among all `r nrow(comments)` comments.}
Most frequent words: `r tex_escape(frequent_text)`. Frequency does not establish endorsement.\par
\textbf{Context matters.} Ownership and review appear together (43861845, 43864090); another comment questions the cost of extra responsibility to reviewers (43867077).\par
\posterfinding{posterPaleRose}{Checking appears alongside ownership and trust. Context remains essential.}
\textbf{Foundation.} Barke et al. (2023) motivate the practice categories. O'Brien (2025) cautions against equating reported verification with successful practice.\par
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.239\textwidth}
\postersection{posterTeal}{RQ2 \quad Verification and replies}
\textbf{Is mentioning a specific verification practice associated with receiving a direct reply?}\par
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{outputs/figures/poster/rq2_reply_rates.pdf}\par
\postercaption{Figure 2. Comments with a retained direct reply.}
Difference (specific minus no specific): \textbf{`r sprintf("%+.2f", rq2$difference_pp)` percentage points}.\par
Yates-corrected $\chi^2(1)=`r formatC(unname(rq2$test$statistic),digits=3,format="f")`$, \textbf{$p=`r formatC(rq2$test$p.value,digits=4,format="f")`$}. Smallest expected count: `r round(min(rq2$expected),1)`.\par
The test does not detect an association. Author and thread dependence weaken inference. A large p-value does not prove no relationship.\par
\vspace{3mm}
\postersection{posterGreen}{RQ3 \quad Content clusters}
\textbf{Do comments form meaningful lexical groups around responsibility and verification?}\par
Log TF-IDF, L2 normalisation, cosine distance and average-link hierarchical clustering of `r clusters$settings$n_clustered` eligible comments.\par
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{outputs/figures/poster/rq3_diagnostics.pdf}\par
\postercaption{Figure 3. Separation and size diagnostics for $k=2$--$8$.}
Selected $k=`r clusters$selected_k`$`r if (clusters$settings$used_fallback) " as a diagnostic fallback" else ""`; mean silhouette \textbf{`r formatC(clusters$settings$selected_mean_silhouette,digits=3,format="f")`}. Cluster sizes: \textbf{`r paste(as.integer(cluster_sizes),collapse=" and ")`}.\par
\posterfinding{posterPaleGreen}{`r if (clusters$settings$used_fallback || clusters$settings$selected_mean_silhouette < 0.05) "Weak, unbalanced separation does not support stable thematic groups." else "Interpret the lexical groups cautiously and check their content in context."`}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.239\textwidth}
\postersection{posterBurgundy}{RQ4 \quad Who and what gets replies?}
\textbf{How are replies structured, and how do they connect to content clusters?}\par
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{outputs/figures/poster/rq4_full_network.pdf}\par
\postercaption{Figure 4. Full directed author reply network. Nodes have equal size; an arrow goes from replying author to parent author.}
\textbf{`r net_value("Network authors")` authors \quad `r net_value("Unique directed author pairs")` directed pairs}\par
`r net_value("Matched reply events")` matched reply events. The largest weak component contains `r net_value("Largest weak component")` authors (`r round(100*net_value("Largest weak component share"),1)`\%). `r net_value("Authors outside graph")` corpus authors have no retained between-author edge.\par
\textbf{Two structural measures}\par
\begin{tabular*}{\linewidth}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}lrr@{}}
Author & In-degree & Betweenness\\
\hline
`r tex_escape(top_authors$author[1])` & `r top_authors$indegree[1]` & `r formatC(top_authors$betweenness[1],digits=4,format="f")`\\
`r tex_escape(top_authors$author[2])` & `r top_authors$indegree[2]` & `r formatC(top_authors$betweenness[2],digits=4,format="f")`\\
\end{tabular*}\par
\postercaption{Table 1. Distinct replying authors and directed, unweighted, normalised betweenness in the full graph.}
\textbf{Content bridge.} Comments receiving replies by lexical group: `r bridge_text`. Weak and unequal clusters prevent a reliable thematic comparison.\par
\posterfinding{posterPaleRose}{Reply prominence describes structural position. It does not establish expertise, approval or influence.}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.239\textwidth}
\postersection{posterGreen}{Main findings}
\textbf{Content.} The selected discussions connect checking code with ownership, review and trust.\par
\textbf{Response.} Specific-practice comments have a slightly lower observed reply rate. The exploratory test supplies no clear evidence of an association.\par
\textbf{Structure.} Most network participants share one large weak component, while lexical clustering separates comments poorly.\par
\posterfinding{posterPaleTeal}{The strongest evidence is descriptive: what these participants discuss and who replies to whom. Stronger claims require broader data and better measurement.}
\vspace{3mm}
\postersection{posterTeal}{Limits and next steps}
Five selected, uneven threads cannot represent all programmers or workplace behaviour.\par
Thread and author dependence, ambiguous text, deleted or missing parents, and short comments constrain inference.\par
RQ2 uses `r specific$n` TRUE and `r no_practice$n` FALSE labels, reported as created using code in Excel. The R ID list reproduces them; the original Excel rule remains uninspected.\par
Broader thread sampling, documented annotation and contextual checks should precede stronger substantive conclusions.\par
\vspace{3mm}
\postersection{posterBurgundy}{Reproducibility and sources}
Frozen input data, keyed joins, R scripts, parameters and complete results accompany the report.\par
```
